_comment: READ BEFORE CHANGING floorHeight OR gapBetweenFloors.
Their sum is the floor-to-floor PITCH, now 20 + 2 = 22 (Gottsch, 2026-08-27, backlog #29
stage 2). The pitch is the exact distance every entrance and transition template has to span.
THE SHIPPED TEMPLATES DO NOT SPAN 22 YET. They are cut for the old pitch of 12, and they are
being re-authored: stairs_1 and ladder1 carry their two door markers 12 apart and cannot be
stretched, the stairs_2 chain only lands on multiples of 6, and the entrance's bottom door
marker DEFINES floor 0's walking plane. Until the new ones land, a generated dungeon has
transitions that stop short -- expected, and the reason TransitionSpanTest is now a release
gate (./gradlew releaseCheck) rather than part of `test`.
Watch the log for [D2-PITCH] and [D2-SPAN]. Every other field in this file is safe to tune.
//sinkOffset: How far the walking plane sits UP into its own floor's slab -- the depth a sunken pit has to
sink into (backlog #3). SHIPPED AT 0, which makes the whole mechanism arithmetically absent.
It is bought from the CEILING, not from the descent. A floor owns exactly floorHeight blocks
either way; sinkOffset just moves the boundary inside that budget, leaving
floorHeight - sinkOffset above the walking plane and sinkOffset below it. So the floor-to-floor
pitch does NOT move and no transition template has to be re-cut to allow pits -- which is the
whole reason pits are separable from the floorHeight raise rather than blocked behind it.
5 as of 2026-08-27, bought by raising floorHeight to 20: a 15-block ceiling budget for
authored rooms, 5 for pits, and a
transition drop of 22. It trades one-for-one against room height, so raising this without
raising floorHeight takes the height straight back out of the rooms; the file fails to load if
it leaves less headroom than a roomHeightBand asks for.
//roomHeightBands: UNCHANGED by the floorHeight raise, deliberately (Gottsch, 2026-08-27). The 15-block ceiling
budget is headroom for AUTHORED rooms -- a template may be cut 15 high and now fits. A
PROCEDURAL room stays capped at 10: a tall empty box is a worse room than a short one, and
what makes height worth having is content, which a template has and a rolled room does not.
The slack above a procedural room costs nothing -- unused floor height is unexcavated stone,
not empty volume, and is invisible in play.
The taper itself is #51: the ceiling FALLS as the footprint grows, so a 7x7 may be a shaft
